authorities.name: Bhasin v. Hrynew
authorities.judge_or_panel: Cromwell J (McLachlin CJ, LeBel, Abella, Rothstein, Karakatsanis, Wagner JJ concurring)
authorities.proposition: Recognises good faith contractual performance as a general organizing principle of the common law of contract, and, as one concrete manifestation of it, a new common law duty of honest performance applying to all contracts: parties must not lie or otherwise knowingly mislead each other about matters directly linked to the performance of the contract. This is not an implied term but a general doctrine of contract law operating irrespective of the parties' intentions - they cannot contract out of it. On the facts, a party breached this duty by acting dishonestly in exercising a non-renewal clause.
authorities.verification_note: The researching agent fetched this directly from the Supreme Court's own official decisions database via a genuine browser session (not a proxy), quoting paragraphs 33, 63, 73-75, and 93-94 verbatim. This session's own independent re-fetch of the same SCC URL returned HTTP 403; paragraph 73's exact wording was instead independently corroborated via WebSearch against a genuine secondary-source quotation.

authorities.name: C.M. Callow Inc. v. Zollinger
authorities.judge_or_panel: Kasirer J (Wagner CJ, Abella, Karakatsanis, Martin JJ concurring); Brown J concurring in result; Côté J dissenting
authorities.proposition: Confirms and extends Bhasin's duty of honest performance: it applies not only to the performance of one's own obligations but to the exercise of one's contractual rights (here, a unilateral termination clause). 'Knowingly misleading' conduct is not confined to spoken lies - it can include half-truths, omissions, and even silence, depending on the circumstances, so long as that operates as active deception rather than mere passive non-disclosure of a material fact. On the facts, a party breached the duty by knowingly misleading the other into believing an agreement would not be terminated, even though the required notice period was technically satisfied.
authorities.verification_note: The researching agent fetched this directly from the Supreme Court's own official decisions database via the same genuine browser-session method, quoting paragraphs 2, 5, 42, and 91 verbatim. This session's own independent re-fetch of the same SCC URL returned HTTP 403; not independently re-confirmed at the pinpoint level by this session, recorded at VERIFIED_SECONDARY_SOURCE consistent with the parallel treatment of the Bhasin node.

edges.verified_via: C.M. Callow v. Zollinger, 2020 SCC 45, paras 2, 5, 42, 91, per the researching agent's SCC-site browser-session fetch: expressly applies Bhasin's organizing-principle framework, extending the duty of honest performance to the exercise of contractual rights and clarifying that misleading conduct can include half-truths, omissions, or silence operating as active deception.

what_this_is_not: Two nodes forming a single doctrinal line on the duty of honest performance - Bhasin creates the duty, Callow defines how far 'misleading' conduct reaches. Deliberately excludes Quebec (a distinct civil-law jurisdiction for private law, covered separately in this repository). Does not cover unconscionability, undue influence, the broader good-faith doctrine beyond honest performance, or any other Canadian common-law Contract Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
